sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio model pricing — directly fetched Prime row
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 by direct HTTPS HTML fetch. The China (Beijing) Qwen-Max pricing table contains qwen3.8-max-prime immediately before qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-max-0902, explicitly links the Prime row to /help/en/model-studio/prime-mode (Fast mode (Prime)), and lists thinking/non-thinking modes through 1M input tokens. The search page extractor still omits this row, but it is present in the fetched HTML. This identifies Prime as a documented Max serving mode; it does not identify an exact dated weight snapshot.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio: Fast mode
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The October 11 Fast mode guide describes an API mode with 1.5–2x standard output TPS, token billing and separate model identifiers that enable the mode without additional parameters. The current supported-model table omits Qwen3.8-Max-Prime, but the exact Prime pricing row links here. The guide does not describe a newly trained, distilled, pruned or expert-expanded model.

sources.title: qwen3.8-max Model Info
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Alibaba directly describes the hosted qwen3.8-max as a 2.4-trillion-parameter MoE flagship with native image/text/video input. It lists qwen3.8-max-0902 (alias qwen3.8-max-2026-09-02) as an upgraded snapshot. This is a published nominal specification of hosted Max, not only the separate open text checkpoint. The page does not identify Prime’s exact dated snapshot.

release_date.note: Fresh full-page checks of Alibaba Model Studio release history, QwenCloud’s native model changelog/news, exact Prime pricing row and the Prime-mode guide do not establish an initial Prime launch date. The dated native changelog covers Max, Max-0902 and regional expansions without a Prime launch entry. open_weights.note: Prime is documented as a hosted serving SKU. The public Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B checkpoint is not demonstrated to be the exact Prime weights; no explicit developer statement about the exact Prime checkpoint’s weight availability was located. Clear the categorical baseline assertion pending exact mapping.

license.note: No standalone weight license is documented for Prime. The separately published Qwen3.8-Max license for 2.4T-A95B cannot be assigned to Prime without an exact weight mapping; API service terms are not a weight license.

parameters_b.note: Nominal 2.4T (2400B), inferred for the developer-documented Fast mode serving variant of Qwen3.8 Max. Alibaba’s exact Prime pricing row links to its Fast mode guide, whose Chinese version says capabilities and limits match the original model; Alibaba and QwenCloud directly publish 2.4T for hosted Max. Vercel independently corroborates retained 2.4T MoE architecture. No structural change was disclosed in the sources checked. This is a nominal model-size inference from the documented serving relationship, not an exact deployed tensor count, a claim about auxiliary service parameters, or proof of a particular Max/0902 snapshot. The missing exact snapshot no longer invalidates the supported nominal size.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 95B active, independently published for hosted Qwen3.8-Max by its developer announcement and QwenCloud news, and inferred for its documented Fast mode serving variant using the same relationship as the total count. This is separately sourced, not calculated from total parameters or expert ratios. Prime has no separate active-count disclosure or exact snapshot mapping; no pruning, changed expert routing, expert expansion or added modality is documented for the mode. Retain the developer’s nominal active count without asserting exact per-token/component accounting.

architecture.note: MoE follows the same documented serving-mode inheritance used for the nominal counts: Alibaba identifies qwen3.8-max-prime as Fast mode, describes Max as MoE, and describes the mode as matching the original capabilities/limits. Vercel corroborates retention of the 2.4T MoE architecture. The precise internal hybrid-attention configuration and exact dated checkpoint are not inferred from the separate open release.

context_window.note: The live Alibaba endpoint metadata on OpenRouter explicitly reports 1,000,000 context tokens. This verifies the provider-documented interface limit, not a generation test.

modalities.note: Live exact-endpoint metadata documents these input and output modalities. No modality is inherited solely from the standard Max record.

patch.description: Fast mode API variant of Qwen3.8 Max with a one-million-token context and text, image and video input.
patch.notes: Prime is Alibaba’s documented Fast mode API SKU for Qwen3.8 Max. Nominal 2400B total and 95B active parameters, and MoE architecture, are inferred from that serving-mode relationship and the developer’s published hosted Max specifications. The exact Prime pricing row is present in the directly fetched October 27 HTML and links to Fast mode; the Chinese guide states the original capabilities and limits are retained. No structural changes are disclosed in the checked sources. Vercel’s retained-2.4T-MoE description is corroborating provider evidence. These are nominal model specifications, not a tensor census or an auxiliary-service count. Exact Prime-to-Max/0902 snapshot identity, weight availability and the open checkpoint’s license remain unresolved. September 23, 2026 remains the verified OpenRouter listing date rather than a confirmed earliest public release. Interface capabilities remain documented by the exact Alibaba endpoint metadata without inference testing. A fresh check of the native release logs, official news and exact pricing/Prime guide found no dated original Prime launch announcement.
